model.name: pvmaps
model.desc: Simulates the energy yield potential of a solar farm (fixed-tilt, tracking, or ground-sculpted vertical bifacial) at a given location, based on module and array design parameters.

lat.desc: Latitude of the solar farm. Positive for North, negative for South.

lon.desc: Longitude of the solar farm. Positive for East, negative for West.

module.cell_tech.desc: Solar cell technology used by the module.

module.height.desc: Physical height of a single module.

module.stc_eff.direct.desc: Module's direct-irradiance collection efficiency under standard test conditions.

module.stc_eff.diffuse.desc: Module's diffuse-irradiance collection efficiency under standard test conditions.

module.tcoeff.desc: Module power temperature coefficient -- how much module power output drops per degree of temperature rise.

array.config.desc: Array mounting configuration: 'fixed' tilt, sun-'tracking', or 'GSVBF' (ground-sculpted vertical bifacial).

array.tilt.desc: Tilt angle of the array relative to horizontal.

array.azimuth.desc: Array facing direction. 90 = East/West facing, 180 = North/South facing.

array.albedo.desc: Ground surface reflectivity beneath and around the array.

array.gsHeight.desc: Ground-sculpting height. Only meaningful when array.config is 'GSVBF'; not used for 'fixed' or 'tracking' configs.

array.elevation.desc: Height of the array above the ground.

output._note: Confirmed against a real `output` struct dump from simulate(). Fields below marked confidence:low are structurally confirmed (shape/dtype from the real dump) but their exact meaning is inferred, not verified against source -- treat with caution until confirmed against the .m source or Jabir. Only yearly_yield, monthly_yield, daily_yield, and yield_unit are currently extracted by pvmaps/matlab_runner.py; everything else here is present in the raw MATLAB struct but currently discarded by the Python wrapper.

yearly_yield.unit: kWh/m (per meter of row length, not areal)
yearly_yield.desc: Total simulated energy yield for the year. Confidence: high.

monthly_yield.unit: kWh/m (per meter of row length, not areal)
monthly_yield.shape: array of 12, one value per calendar month (Jan-Dec)
monthly_yield.desc: Simulated energy yield for each month of the year. Confidence: high.

daily_yield.unit: kWh/m (per meter of row length, not areal)
daily_yield.shape: array of 12 -- despite the name, this is NOT 365 per-day values. Each entry is that month's average daily yield.
daily_yield.desc: Average daily energy yield per month, verified against a real dump to equal monthly_yield[i] / days_in_month[i] exactly (e.g. Jan: 102.1223 / 31 = 3.2943, matching daily_yield[0]). Do not treat as a per-calendar-day series -- there is no way to recover an individual day's (e.g. July 7th's) yield from this field. This is the field responsible for a past fabrication bug where the LLM invented specific daily values. Confidence: high.

yield_unit.desc: Unit string for the yield fields, as returned by the simulator (e.g. 'kwh/m'). Confidence: high.

time.shape: array of 12 (one per month), each a column vector whose length varies by month (e.g. 609 for Jan, 848 for Jun, 593 for Dec) -- length tracks day-length seasonality, consistent with one representative simulated day per month at some sub-hourly resolution
time.desc: Per-month array of simulation timesteps for that month's representative day(s). Exact clock convention (minutes since midnight vs since sunrise) not confirmed. Confidence: low.

opt_tracking_angle.shape: array of 12, each matching that month's time vector length
opt_tracking_angle.desc: Likely the optimal tracking tilt angle at each simulated timestep. Presumably only meaningful when array.config is 'tracking'; behavior for 'fixed'/'GSVBF' unconfirmed. Confidence: low.

opt_power.unit: unknown, likely W or kW -- unconfirmed
opt_power.shape: array of 12, each matching that month's time vector length
opt_power.desc: Likely instantaneous power output at each simulated timestep -- the per-timestep series that monthly_yield is integrated/averaged from. Confidence: low.

opt_p.shape: array of 12, each itself a cell array matching that month's time vector length (one level deeper nested than opt_power)
opt_p.desc: Unknown. Likely a per-timestep breakdown of opt_power into components (e.g. direct/diffuse/reflected contributions), but this is a guess -- no source confirmation. Confidence: very low.

solarnoon.shape: array of 12, one value per month (e.g. Jan: 304, Jun: 423, Dec: 296)
solarnoon.desc: Likely the clock time of solar noon for each month's representative day. Confidence: low.

simdat.shape: array of 12, each a nested struct with unknown internal fields
simdat.desc: Detailed per-month simulation data, present because input.sim.save_simdat=true. Internal structure not inspected. Confidence: very low.

power_mat.unit: unknown, likely W or kW -- unconfirmed
power_mat.shape: array of 12, each a (timesteps x 50) matrix -- rows match that month's time vector length, 50 columns of unknown meaning (possibly spatial discretization points along a row, or per-module positions)
power_mat.desc: Likely a spatially-resolved power profile (e.g. across ground/row position) at each timestep -- candidate data source for visualizing self-shading or ground irradiance patterns. Confidence: low.

sim_params.shape: single nested struct, internal fields unknown
sim_params.desc: Likely echoes the simulator configuration actually used for the run (resolution, quickSim flag, etc.). Internal structure not inspected. Confidence: very low.

warnings.desc: Not part of the raw MATLAB struct -- synthesized by pvmaps/matlab_runner.py, currently always hardcoded to empty. Confidence: high (about the wrapper's behavior, not about MATLAB).

final_inputs.shape: object with a fixed subset of keys: model, lat, lon, panel_type, tracking, tilt, pitch
final_inputs.desc: Not part of the raw MATLAB struct -- built manually by pvmaps/matlab_runner.py as a partial echo of the inputs. Incomplete -- does not include albedo, azimuth, elevation, or gsHeight even though those were part of the input. Confidence: high (about the wrapper's behavior, not about MATLAB).
